sentence: She has lived in Penang ____ 2019.
explanation: Use 'since' with a starting point in time (2019). 'For' is used with a length of time, such as 'for five years'.

sentence: Neither the manager nor the assistants ____ aware of the change.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. 'Assistants' is plural, so the verb is 'were'.

sentence: If I ____ about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
explanation: This is a third conditional about the past: 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle'. 'Knew' belongs to the second conditional.

sentence: The report, together with its appendices, ____ due on Friday.
explanation: The subject is 'the report' (singular). Phrases such as 'together with' or 'along with' do not make the subject plural.

sentence: She is interested ____ communication research.
explanation: The adjective 'interested' is always followed by 'in'.

sentence: By the time we arrived, the lecture ____.
explanation: The lecture started before another past action (our arrival), so the past perfect 'had started' shows the earlier action.

sentence: Each of the students ____ submitted a draft.
explanation: 'Each' is the subject and it is singular, so it takes 'has', even though 'students' is plural.

sentence: This is ____ most persuasive argument in the essay.
explanation: Superlatives such as 'most persuasive' take the definite article 'the' because they identify one specific item.

sentence: I look forward to ____ from you.
explanation: In 'look forward to', the word 'to' is a preposition, not part of an infinitive, so it is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

sentence: Hardly ____ the room when the lights went out.
explanation: When a sentence begins with a negative adverb such as 'hardly', the subject and auxiliary are inverted: 'Hardly had she entered...when'.

sentence: There ____ fewer complaints this year than last year.
explanation: The real subject is 'fewer complaints', which is plural and in the past, so 'there were' is correct.

sentence: We had ____ time left, so we skipped the summary.
explanation: 'Time' is uncountable, so it takes 'little' rather than 'few'. 'Little' (without 'a') stresses that the amount was not enough, which explains why the summary was skipped.

sentence: The university has updated ____ website.
explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form. 'It's' means 'it is' or 'it has', and 'its'' does not exist in standard English.

sentence: She speaks English ____ than her brother.
explanation: The word describes how she speaks, so it must be an adverb (fluently). Comparisons of long adverbs use 'more...than'.

sentence: Unless you ____ the deadline, your work will not be graded.
explanation: After 'unless' (and 'if') in a first conditional, use the present simple, not 'will'.

sentence: This is the lecturer ____ book I reviewed.
explanation: 'Whose' shows possession (the lecturer's book). 'Who's' means 'who is' or 'who has'.

sentence: The participants, ____ were interviewed in person, gave detailed answers.
explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of 'were interviewed' and refers to people, so 'who' is correct. 'Whom' is used for objects.

sentence: To ____ it may concern,
explanation: In this fixed formal opening, the pronoun is the object of the preposition 'to', so the object form 'whom' is used.

sentence: I wish I ____ more time to edit the report.
explanation: 'Wish' about a present situation is followed by the past simple ('I wish I had'), which shows the situation is unreal.

sentence: The more you practise, ____ your writing becomes.
explanation: The pattern 'the + comparative..., the + comparative' shows two things changing together: 'The more..., the better...'.

sentence: She has been working here ____ three years.
explanation: 'For' is used with a length of time (three years). 'Since' needs a starting point, such as 'since 2023'.

sentence: He is used to ____ early for his shift.
explanation: 'Be used to' means 'be accustomed to'. Here 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund (waking).

sentence: Not only ____ the report late, but it was also incomplete.
explanation: When a sentence begins with 'Not only', the subject and verb are inverted. The main verb is 'be' in the past, so it becomes 'Not only was the report late'.

sentence: The results were ____ than we expected.
explanation: The comparative form of 'bad' is irregular: bad, worse, worst. 'Than' signals a comparison, so 'worse' is needed.

sentence: Either the students or the teacher ____ the keys.
explanation: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'The teacher' is singular, so 'has' is correct.

sentence: She asked me where ____.
explanation: In reported (indirect) questions, use normal statement word order, with no 'do' or 'did': 'She asked me where I lived'.

sentence: The survey ____ by 200 employees last month.
explanation: The survey did not do the action; employees completed it. This needs the passive, and 'last month' requires the past: 'was completed'.

sentence: ____ the rain, the event went ahead.
explanation: 'Despite' is followed directly by a noun ('the rain'). 'Although' and 'even though' need a full clause, and 'in spite' needs 'of'.

sentence: He didn't attend the briefing, and ____ did I.
explanation: To agree with a negative statement, use 'neither + auxiliary + subject': 'and neither did I'. 'So did I' agrees with a positive statement.

sentence: Our team has ____ advice for new interns.
explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable, so it cannot take 'a' or 'many'. Use 'some' or no determiner.

sentence: Please send the files to Aisha and ____.
explanation: The pronoun is the object of the preposition 'to', so use the object form 'me'. Test it by removing 'Aisha and': 'send the files to me'.

sentence: The number of applicants ____ increased this year.
explanation: 'The number of' refers to a single figure, so it takes a singular verb: 'The number...has increased'.

sentence: A number of applicants ____ withdrawn.
explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' or 'many', so it takes a plural verb: 'A number of applicants have withdrawn'.

sentence: If it ____ tomorrow, we will move the talk indoors.
explanation: In a first conditional, the 'if' clause uses the present simple even when it refers to the future.

sentence: The manager, along with two supervisors, ____ attending the workshop.
explanation: The subject is 'the manager' (singular). 'Along with two supervisors' is extra information and does not change agreement.

sentence: He has ____ finished the analysis; only the conclusion remains.
explanation: 'Almost' means 'nearly' and modifies the verb 'finished'. 'Most' is not used as an adverb this way, and 'at most' means 'no more than'.

sentence: This is the ____ interesting talk I have attended.
explanation: 'The...I have attended' compares this talk with all others, so the superlative 'most' is required.

sentence: Their argument is weak because it ____ on a single source.
explanation: The subject 'it' is third person singular, so the present simple verb takes -s: 'relies'.

sentence: We need to discuss the issue ____ it becomes a crisis.
explanation: 'Before' shows that the discussion should happen earlier than the crisis. 'Until' would mean continuing up to the crisis.

sentence: She stopped ____ to her colleague because the meeting had started.
explanation: 'Stop + -ing' means to end an activity. 'Stop + to-infinitive' means to pause in order to do something, which does not fit the meaning here.

sentence: I remember ____ the email, but I cannot find it now.
explanation: 'Remember + -ing' refers to a memory of something already done. 'Remember to' refers to a task you must not forget.

sentence: Remember ____ the door when you leave.
explanation: This is a reminder about a future task, so use 'remember + to-infinitive'.

sentence: The findings ____ in the next issue of the journal.
explanation: The findings are not doing the publishing; they receive the action. The future passive 'will be published' is correct.

sentence: ____ you need help, ask the librarian.
explanation: 'Should you need help' is a formal inverted conditional meaning 'If you need help'.

sentence: She arrived ____ than expected.
explanation: 'Early' forms its comparative with -er: early, earlier, earliest. 'Than' shows a comparison is needed.

sentence: The audit was ____ by the head of department.
explanation: The passive needs 'was + past participle'. The past participle of 'oversee' is 'overseen'; 'oversaw' is the simple past.

sentence: My colleague and ____ presented the findings.
explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject, so the subject form 'I' is correct. Test it by removing 'my colleague and': 'I presented'.

sentence: It's time we ____ a decision.
explanation: After 'It's time + subject', English uses the past simple to suggest that the action should already be happening.

sentence: Phones must stay silent ____ the examination.
explanation: 'Throughout' means 'during the whole of'. It is written as one word.

sentence: Between you and ____, the proposal needs more work.
explanation: 'Between' is a preposition, so both pronouns after it must be in the object form: 'between you and me'.

sentence: The scissors ____ on the desk.
explanation: Nouns such as 'scissors', 'trousers' and 'glasses' are plural in form and take plural verbs.

sentence: Mathematics ____ my strongest subject at school.
explanation: Subjects such as mathematics, physics and economics end in -s but are singular, so they take a singular verb.

sentence: Had I known, I ____ you.
explanation: 'Had I known' is an inverted third conditional (If I had known). The result clause needs 'would have + past participle'.

sentence: She is the kind of person ____ you can trust.
explanation: The pronoun is the object of 'trust' and refers to a person, so 'whom' (or 'who' / 'that' in informal use) is correct. 'Which' is for things.

sentence: He was accused ____ plagiarism.
explanation: The verb 'accuse' is followed by 'of': accuse someone of something.

sentence: The lecture was cancelled ____ the lecturer's illness.
explanation: 'Due to' is followed by a noun phrase. 'Because' would need 'of' or a full clause, and 'despite' and 'although' show contrast, not cause.

sentence: This method is different ____ the one we used last year.
explanation: 'Different from' is the most widely accepted form in formal writing. 'Then' is a time word and is often confused with 'than'.

sentence: She is good ____ summarising long reports.
explanation: The adjective 'good' is followed by 'at' when it describes a skill.

sentence: Our survey received ____ responses than last year's.
explanation: 'Responses' is a countable plural noun, so formal English uses 'fewer'. 'Less' is used with uncountable nouns such as 'less time'.

sentence: The policy, ____ was introduced in 2024, has reduced complaints.
explanation: This is a non-defining clause (extra information between commas), and it refers to a thing, so 'which' is required. 'That' is not used after a comma in this way.

sentence: The new policy will ____ all full-time staff.
explanation: 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning 'to influence'. 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning 'a result'.

sentence: The training had a positive ____ on morale.
explanation: A noun is needed after 'a positive'. 'Effect' is the noun meaning 'result' or 'influence'.

sentence: Please ____ the attached document for details.
explanation: The verb 'refer' needs the preposition 'to' when it means 'look at for information'.

sentence: Her speech was so ____ that the audience stayed silent long after it ended.
explanation: Adjectives ending in -ing describe what causes a feeling (the speech). Adjectives ending in -ed describe how people feel (the audience was moved).

sentence: From her tone, I ____ that she was unhappy.
explanation: The listener infers (draws a conclusion); the speaker implies (suggests something indirectly). Here 'I' am drawing the conclusion.

sentence: We need to ____ the problem before it spreads.
explanation: To 'address' a problem means to start dealing with it. 'Attend' would need 'to', and 'adhere' means to stick to rules.

sentence: The lecturer gave us some useful ____ on our drafts.
explanation: 'Feedback' is uncountable, so it has no plural form and cannot take 'a'.

sentence: She made a ____ decision after weighing every option.
explanation: 'Deliberate' as an adjective means 'carefully considered'. It fits a decision made after weighing every option.

sentence: The two departments ____ closely on the communication audit.
explanation: 'Collaborate' means to work together. 'Collude' also means working together, but secretly and dishonestly, so it is negative.

sentence: The witness ____ the victim's account of events.
explanation: 'Corroborate' means to confirm or support a statement with evidence. It is often confused with 'collaborate'.

sentence: Please be ____ when you share confidential information.
explanation: 'Discreet' means careful and tactful about private matters. 'Discrete' means separate and distinct.

sentence: The survey divided responses into four ____ categories.
explanation: 'Discrete' means separate and distinct, which describes categories. 'Discreet' means careful about privacy.

sentence: The professor's ____ comments helped me improve.
explanation: 'Constructive' feedback is helpful and aims to improve something. It is an adjective, which is needed before the noun 'comments'.

sentence: The questionnaire was designed to ____ honest responses.
explanation: 'Elicit' means to draw out a response or information. 'Illicit' is an adjective meaning illegal.

sentence: The CEO ____ the importance of clear internal communication.
explanation: A past-tense verb is needed. 'Emphasised' (American spelling: emphasized) means 'stressed'. 'Empathised' means 'shared someone's feelings'.

sentence: The meeting was ____ until next Tuesday.
explanation: 'Postpone' means to move to a later time. 'Prepone' (to move earlier) is used in Indian English but is not standard in British or American English.

sentence: The colour scheme ____ the minimalist layout well.
explanation: 'Complement' means to go well with or complete something. 'Compliment' means to praise.

sentence: Her explanation was ____ and easy to follow.
explanation: 'Concise' means brief but clear. The other options are nouns or have unrelated meanings.

sentence: The team reached a ____ after a long debate.
explanation: 'Consensus' means general agreement. A 'census' is an official count of a population.

sentence: Our findings ____ that staff prefer face-to-face meetings.
explanation: A main verb is needed after the plural subject 'findings'. 'Suggest' is the right verb for cautiously presenting results.

sentence: Her tone was polite but ____; she would not change her decision.
explanation: After the linking verb 'was', an adjective is needed. 'Firm' means strong and not willing to change.

sentence: The new manager is very ____; she always listens to staff concerns.
explanation: 'Approachable' means friendly and easy to talk to.

sentence: The instructions were ____, so many staff misunderstood them.
explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation, which explains the misunderstanding.

sentence: He has a ____ for exaggerating small problems.
explanation: 'A tendency for' or 'a tendency to' describes a habit or likely behaviour.

sentence: The memo was written in a ____ tone, which upset several employees.
explanation: 'Condescending' means showing that you think you are better than others. It is the -ing adjective that describes the tone.

sentence: Students must ____ to the referencing guidelines.
explanation: 'Adhere to' means to follow rules closely. 'Adherent' is a noun or adjective, not a verb.

sentence: She ____ a valuable contribution to the project.
explanation: The natural collocation is 'make a contribution'. Collocations are word pairs that native speakers commonly use together.

sentence: Could you ____ me a favour?
explanation: The fixed expression is 'do someone a favour'.

sentence: The speaker ____ attention to the gap in the research.
explanation: The collocation is 'draw attention to'. The past tense of 'draw' is 'drew'.

sentence: Let's ____ a brief look at the figures.
explanation: The collocation is 'take a look' (or 'have a look' in British English).

sentence: The new system has ____ efficiency by twenty percent.
explanation: 'Increase' can take an object (increased efficiency). 'Rise' cannot take an object; something rises by itself.

sentence: Prices ____ sharply last quarter.
explanation: 'Rise' (rose, risen) has no object: prices rose. 'Raise' needs an object: the company raised prices. 'Risen' needs 'have'.

sentence: Please ____ the books on the shelf.
explanation: 'Lay' means to put something down and takes an object (the books). 'Lie' means to rest in a flat position and has no object.

sentence: I need to ____ down after the long meeting.
explanation: 'Lie down' means to rest your body in a flat position. It takes no object, so 'lay' is incorrect here.

sentence: The proposal was rejected ____ its high cost.
explanation: 'Because of' is followed by a noun phrase ('its high cost'). 'Because' alone needs a full clause.

sentence: She is ____ to take the lead on this project.
explanation: 'Eligible' means having the right qualifications or meeting the conditions. 'Legible' and 'illegible' describe handwriting.

sentence: His handwriting is so messy that it is ____.
explanation: 'Illegible' means impossible to read. 'Ineligible' means not qualified.

sentence: The ____ of the report is to evaluate internal communication.
explanation: 'Purpose' is the noun meaning 'aim'. 'Propose' is a verb, and a 'porpoise' is a sea animal.

sentence: We should ____ his advice and revise the introduction.
explanation: To 'heed' advice means to pay attention to it and follow it.

sentence: The lecturer was ____ by the quality of the final submissions.
explanation: 'Impressed' (-ed) describes how a person feels. 'Impressive' (-ive) describes the thing that causes the feeling.

sentence: The ____ reason for the delay was a staff shortage.
explanation: 'Principal' as an adjective means 'main'. 'Principle' is a noun meaning a rule or belief.

sentence: The office ordered new ____, including pens and envelopes.
explanation: 'Stationery' (with -ery) means writing materials. 'Stationary' (with -ary) means not moving.

sentence: Several staff ____ the dress code by wearing sandals.
explanation: 'Flout' means to openly ignore a rule. 'Flaunt' means to show something off proudly.

sentence: The writer used a striking ____ to compare memory to a river.
explanation: A 'metaphor' describes one thing as if it were another to suggest a likeness.
